### Repro for the intermittent connect error
Stack trace from server A:
``` panic: nats: connection closed
goroutine 42 [running]: github.com/example/relay.(*client).publish(0xc0001a8000, 0xc0002b4c00, 0x40, 0x40) /src/relay/client.go:118 +0x2a4 github.com/example/relay.Worker.run(...) /src/relay/worker.go:76 created by main.main /src/main.go:48 +0x110 ```
Minimal Go repro (note the shift: `1 << 20` publishes exhaust the pool):
```go cfg := relay.Config{URL: "nats://nats:4222", Subject: "cg.post"} c, err := relay.Dial(cfg) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("dial: %v", err) } for i := 0; i < 1<<20; i++ { _ = c.Publish([]byte("x")) } ```
Query I used to confirm duplicate outbox rows (`AND` + `HAVING count(*) > 1`):
```sql SELECT post_id, count(*) AS n FROM relay_outbox WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour' AND acked_at IS NULL GROUP BY post_id HAVING count(*) > 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20; ```
And the one-liner I ran to reproduce (bash `&` backgrounds each post):
```sh for i in $(seq 1 1000); do mmctl post create --team test-a --channel town-square --message "load $i" & done wait ```
Here's the raw XML frame that tripped the decoder (note the missing `<Timestamp>`):
```xml <CrossguardMessage xmlns="urn:mattermost-crossguard"> <Type>crossguard_post</Type> <!-- Timestamp element missing, which is what caused the nil deref --> <PostMessage> <PostID>deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefda</PostID> <MessageText>hello & goodbye</MessageText> </PostMessage> </CrossguardMessage> ```
If anyone can run this against `high.test` with a fresh Azurite and grab the `relay_writer_blocked_seconds` metric, that would help narrow it down.
